rows.title: CSU faculty union refuses retirement buyouts
rows.standfirst: One of CT’s largest faculty unions won’t take part in a retirement incentive program officials are counting on to close the CSCU deficit.

rows.title: Lamont negotiates big pay hike for CT home health aides
rows.standfirst: The tentative 3-year contract would boost minimum wages for home health aides by 26% to $23 per hour by the 2025-26 fiscal year.

rows.title: Lamont, unions agree on 2.5% wage hike plus step increase
rows.standfirst: All employees would get the general 2.5% increase on July 1. A step hike would be applied midway through next fiscal year, on Jan. 1.

rows.title: Plan to cut CT’s transportation debt could offer more than savings
rows.standfirst: The goal is to save about $70M in debt service payments and use the money to speed up the rebuild of CT’s aging transportation infrastructure.

rows.title: Push for $600-per-child CT income tax credit faces big hurdles
rows.standfirst: Dozens of legislators have co-sponsored bills to help establish a per-child tax credit, and about 100 people testified on them last week.

rows.title: CT’s big budget question: How much COVID relief money remains?
rows.standfirst: Legislators working on CT’s budget don’t know how much ARPA funding is left, nor do they know when Lamont’s administration will tell them.

rows.title: CT state agencies ordered to tally unspent ARPA funds
rows.standfirst: The directive from Gov. Lamont’s budget director was issued hours after The Connecticut Mirror published a story about legislators’ concerns.

rows.title: CT employee raises could hinder aid for higher education
rows.standfirst: CT higher ed officials say raises for state employees could complicate their already uphill climb to close deficits and preserve programs.

rows.title: CT lawmakers seeking new options to work around budget cap
rows.standfirst: CT lawmakers have spent millions in recent years outside the ‘fiscal guardrails,’ but these temporary wells are quickly running dry.

rows.title: Few details about Prospect Medical’s $12 million tax cut
rows.standfirst: A tax break extended to Prospect Medical Holdings will be paid back, top CT officials said, though details were few.

rows.title: Lawmakers hope CT’s big reserves can solve budget dilemma
rows.standfirst: Legislators say the interest from the rainy day fund could solve many problems, but Gov. Ned Lamont says it would violate basic principles.
